detail.longDescription: Hi HN! After we launched our public beta, some of our ex-colleagues tested the approach of creating decision models based on their work artefacts and noticed that it led to fewer back-and-forth cycles to clarify details and greater productivity in their daily routine. The market for professionals has a downside: the problem of scaling the business model. You physically can't have more hours in a day, and as a professional, you manage the flow of incoming clients through pricing and balancing your personal time. The AI market has a downside: the problem of model subjectivity. You can set boundaries through "prompt engineering" and say, "Respond as a professional." But after a couple of messages, you'll ask something like, "...maybe doing it this way would be better?" and the model will agree with you. Because the model doesn't have its own point of view. We're solving this problem by creating an expert's decision model. Then another user who needs that expert's expertise can ask it questions and get answers about how the expert would act in that case. From a technical perspective, we initially used a RAG architecture to build expert models. However, this approach (uploading all the artifacts and trying to create a replacement or copy of an expertise) turned out to be a failure. So we took a completely different approach, similar to how you would compare movies from different genres. This led to a significant improvement in the quality of answers.
